entries.note: genesis: free local Tier 1 audit front door; zero network enforced by a socket guard in the audit process and in the scorer-probe subprocess, not asserted in prose

from the first run on a real 103-file project: collapse repeated not-run lines to one per reason, tighten the scorer-candidate filter so validators and test helpers are counted as ruled out rather than reported as scorers, and add the single recommended next step the brief requires

independent tools-on review found the zero-network claim false on 5 of 8 escape routes: shrink the claim to what is enforced, add a preflighted network-namespace sandbox for the probe, close _socket and the ssl-breaking guard, refuse a non-deterministic --scorer, stop relaying exception and stderr text, and turn every silent cap into a printed finding

second review round: classify a module named at runtime as executing and stop presenting the classifier as a boundary, read only the probe's own framed result line through a typed whitelist so a scorer cannot forge a verdict, and bind the project back into the sandbox so a project under /tmp is not reported as a broken scorer

add the approval-gated second tier (scripts/tier2_checks.py): offer mode prints one approval card per applicable check under the same network guard Tier 1 installs and makes no request and spawns no process; run mode touches only the approved checks' named endpoints and writes a receipt the tests compare byte-for-byte against a real listener's log. Transport is X-API-Key plus the SDK's own User-Agent, proven against that listener; the key never reaches a card, a receipt, a command line or an error, and a response echoing it is withheld. Ships the shared economics reference by pointer

after a cross-vendor consult and a customer dogfood run: example-scoring becomes a READER (summary, then dataset-quality only on computed:true) because the compute endpoint returned HTTP 500 and a successful read establishes neither its availability nor a charging boundary; `computed:false` is relayed as not computed and never as permission to POST. Replace the 'what settles it' promises with what the services actually do -- retrieve a verdict if they have one -- and state that a completed run is necessary and not sufficient, with each card carrying what the same check returned on our own run. Add stop-here as a recommendable card so no run is ever recommended merely to make an analysis service answer. Disclose the key header on every card, and keep the agent's own pre-approval interaction-profile fetch out of Tier 1. Run discovery lists project/experiment/run context and auto-selects nothing, names the listing limit, and says a local session id 404s. Document the origin-vs-/api/v1 base-URL split and refuse a base URL carrying a path; relay the plan's evidence_level and objectives orientation verbatim with the advisory-steps warning

independent tools-on review of the Tier 2 commit, six findings with executed probes: (H1) run ids and the service's own experiment ids were interpolated raw into URL paths, so a `..` walked the request to another endpoint while the receipt recorded the unsent string -- every segment is now escaped, a dots-only segment has its dots encoded too, a run id that is not run-id shaped is refused before any request, and the receipt records the path read back off the wire; (H2) one list-runs approval followed however many experiments the server returned -- it is now capped at the page it asked for, with the overflow reported; (M1) project text was printed into both cards unfiltered, so a planted escape sequence rewrote a consent line -- one `printable_text` filter now covers every rendered line of both renderers; (M2) argparse prefix matching made `--appr` an approval the argv scan missed, installing the guard and then taking the run-mode path -- abbreviations are off and the mode is read from the parsed namespace; (L1) the offer header claimed the guard proved no process was spawned, which it cannot -- the two halves are now stated separately and run mode prints the counted processes; (L2) the same field name from two scopes printed as two contradictory lines -- the nested scope is labelled

read a completed traigent-first-run correctly: files under traigent-runs/ are counted on one card line as walkthrough material and never taken as the project's entry point, dataset or scorer (split_walkthrough_files); a two-file holdout layout in the project's own directories (a holdout/heldout/validation/val-named dataset file beside a tuning file) is read as a declared holdout slice for both files with the overlap check run across the pair by normalized input, per-row split markers winning when present (apply_sibling_holdouts); the interpreter probe tries .venv, then .venv-traigent, then the audit's own. New fixture tests/fixtures/first-run-graduate plus four tests shown red before the change. File-name holdout tokens are narrower than the per-row markers: `eval`/`test` in a file name usually name the tuning set, so only holdout/heldout/validation/val declare a holdout by name.

review fix: the guided first run writes its tuning/holdout pair under traigent-runs/, not eval/ - the sibling-holdout reader is documented as a project-directory feature, the walkthrough card line names the first run's reserved slice and who continues from it (holdout_files), a holdout-named file is judged by the holdout minimum only in next_step branch f (holdout_by_name); fixture gains traigent-runs/holdout.jsonl and three tests.

review correction: associate tuning and holdout sibling files when their rows carry split tags, propagate the tagged holdout count, compare normalized inputs across the actual row roles, preserve mixed per-row semantics, and report holdout-filename contradictions instead of relabelling tagged tuning rows; add tagged overlap, tagged no-overlap, mixed-role, and existing untagged regression coverage.

independent rereview correction in the setup-audit script: role precedence is reconciled per row in partially tagged holdout-named files, so explicit holdout rows remain holdout, explicit non-holdout rows remain excluded and diagnosed, and untagged rows inherit the filename holdout role; a real-scanner regression proves the inherited row contributes to both the sibling holdout count and normalized overlap detection. Instructional SKILL.md content and version are unchanged.
